newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond yield curve hammered flat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond yield curve hammered flat.

text.p: The Australian bond yield curve flattened sharply after today's wages data came in at the top end of expectations and was seen lessening the chances of a further policy easing in this cycle.

The three/10-year bond futures yield spread dropped double figures shortly after the data release, which showed average weekly ordinary time earnings rising 1.2 percent in the November quarter against median forecasts for a 0.9 percent rise.
This took the annual rate to 3.9 percent and above the 3.8 percent seen in the August quarter.

The three/10-year bond spread now stands at its lowest level since the start of the year and some 20 basis points below a recent closing high of around 104.5 basis points when speculation of rate cut was at its peak.
The local market also severely underperformed other dollar bloc bonds with the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread spiking to its highest level since mid-January.

U.S. Treasuries had themselves sold off late on Wednesday ahead of Friday's non-farm payrolls and next week's quarterly refunding auctions, and despite the Federal Open Market Committee meeting leaving policy unchanged.
The largest spread move was against Canadian debt, which outpaced the U.S. on Wednesday in anticipation of a well received Canadian Federal budget later this month.
The New Zealand market was closed for a local holiday.
